purpose: Indapamide is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and to reduce fluid buildup (swelling) caused by conditions like heart failure. Lowering high blood pressure helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels. It can be used alone or combined with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Indapamide works by telling your kidneys to remove extra salt and water from your body through your urine. This reduces the amount of fluid in your blood vessels, which lowers the pressure on the walls of your arteries. Think of it like releasing pressure from an overfilled water balloon — less fluid means less pressure.
common_side_effects: Needing to urinate more often (especially early in treatment), dizziness or lightheadedness when standing up quickly, low potassium levels (which may cause muscle cramps or weakness), headache, tiredness, and dry mouth. These often improve as your body adjusts.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, diabetes, or gout, as this medicine can affect those conditions. Low potassium or sodium levels can occur, so your doctor will do blood tests to monitor your levels. Avoid getting dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially other blood pressure drugs or lithium.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1.25 mg taken by mouth once a day, typically in the morning. Your doctor may increase the dose to 2.5 mg per day if needed. Take it in the morning to avoid having to urinate during the night. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed.
